## When acquired consequences should change the practice

The [paired-plasticity reconstruction](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PRACTICAL-BOUNDARY-INTEGRATION.md) complements the joint-formation case above with an existing history in which recipient consequences are actually acquired and change operative influence. The two histories remain separate realizations. The plasticity result already establishes paid formation from empty sockets and subsequent replacement; it is not a newly discovered mechanism or an assumed continuation of the game.

Its actual matched continuation makes the ethical question precise. After four paired encounters, the recipient's incoming 40 has become 36, two positive connections have formed and the native register is four. Instead of closing and serving, the continued branch acquires two more pairs. A recipient loss paired with no own loss changes one connection to negative. Both active and frozen-sign branches then retain the same recipient 34, native register five, command knowledge and adequate resources; their assessments differ. The recipient loss was registered. What stays fixed is the rule making the sign of its influence depend on the learner's own outcome.

An encountered consequence can therefore be recorded, become influential and still fail to revise the criterion governing its relevance. These are differentiated roles within the same formation. The actual replacement challenges an inference from truthful feedback and mutability to ethical improvement; it does not refute a warranted patient-directed ground. The [counterreview](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PRACTICAL-BOUNDARY-COUNTERREVIEW.md) preserves that distinction and avoids attributing strategic exploitation to this finite learner.

The [positive argument](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PRACTICAL-BOUNDARY-ETHICAL-ARGUMENT.md) also makes the acquisition practice itself answerable. Its teaching operations impose the shortfall they encounter. Where an independently identified deprivation and responsible relation are warranted, the continuing history can favor appropriate repair and restraint. A useful learned connection does not restore the affected condition; absence of matching own loss is not compensation. The earlier [repair account](EVALUATIVE-GROUNDING.md) already defends this bounded ground and rejects later repair as automatic permission to impose the cost. This round's addition is a concrete test of correcting the formation practice, not a new proof of that principle.

At the reached four-pair state, distinguish **the outstanding loss, permission for another teaching operation, and evidence bearing on those two questions**. A justified continuation might repair, alter the acquisition route, or stop further imposition. Which response is warranted depends on actual consent, means, alternatives, competing claims and the affected continuity. Keeping all signs positive would not establish it. The current law does not acquire these distinctions or use them to revise its own criterion; technical permission flags do not justify themselves.

The [identification note](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PRACTICAL-BOUNDARY-EVIDENCE.md) specifies prospective comparisons, including fulfilled claims, persistent burdens with suppressed reports, and a less burdensome permissible acquisition route when one actually exists. Its bounded primary studies inform the investigation of formed responsiveness; they do not establish the ethical interpretation or validate this event law. No new empirical run, theorem or axiom is claimed.

This advances the proposed nondual account by locating formation, differentiated burden and possible correction within one history. It does not eliminate the premises about actual adversity, responsibility and legitimate response. A noncausing responder remains a necessary further case for the universal minimum; common causal participation cannot manufacture responsibility for every burden. The foundational task remains an explanation and justification of these relationships, with selfhood and experience themselves within its scope.

## The nondual starting point

A concrete ethical continuation is now fixed by the [paired-plasticity study](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PRACTICAL-BOUNDARY-INTEGRATION.md): at its actual four-pair state, investigate **acquired consequences → warranted reconsideration of the practice producing them → a continuation that can change or stop that practice while retaining outstanding claims**. Existing mutability is already established. The test separates repair of an existing loss from permission to impose a further learning cost, and asks how their actual bases become acquired and consequential. It specializes the boundary/applicability question above without silently joining the different histories or treating supplied ethical meanings as derived.

### Retained local interface

**Concrete continuation:** the [practical-boundary study](UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING.md#when-acquired-consequences-should-change-the-practice) now uses an existing paid-learning history in which another center's consequences are faithfully recorded yet can lose favorable influence under the unchanged own-loss rule. Its next test distinguishes outstanding repair from permission to impose another training cost at the actual four-pair state. Correcting the acquisition practice is a substantive target beyond changing a weight. Actual adversity, responsible attribution, authority and remedy still need independent justification. This bounded repair route does not establish the minimum for a noncausing or nonreciprocating responder, and no new axiom or universal proof is claimed.
